title: Quadratic coefficient graded chart and its geometric branch labels
statement:
Let $F$ be a field, let $a,b,c\in F$ satisfy $a\ne0$ and $b^2-4ac\ne0$, put $q=aX^2+bXY+cY^2$, and set $L=F[Z]/(aZ^2+bZ+c)$ with $z$ the class of $Z$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Give
$$H=F\oplus\bigoplus_{n\ge1}Lt^n\subset L[t]$$
its polynomial degree grading. For every unit $u\in L^\times$, the entire projective spectrum is its single standard chart
$$\operatorname{Proj}H=D_+(ut),\qquad H[(ut)^{-1}]_0\xrightarrow{\sim}L,\quad rt^n/(ut)^n\longmapsto r/u^n$$
for $n\ge1$, with constants mapped by $F\to L$. Here Proj, charts and homogeneous localization use [def-nagata-affine-proj, def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], and spectra use [def-weil-affine-spectrum].
The $F$-algebra $L$ has dimension two and is separable: either it is $F\times F$, or it is a degree-two field extension in which every element is separable over $F$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. For an algebraic closure $\Omega/F$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $r_1,r_2\in\Omega$ be the distinct roots of $aZ^2+bZ+c$. Evaluation induces $L\otimes_F\Omega\cong\Omega\times\Omega$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The two points of $\operatorname{Proj}H$ over $\Omega$ have chart coordinate $z$ equal to $r_1,r_2$ respectively. Under $X\mapsto zt$, $Y\mapsto t$, coefficientwise evaluation of $L[[t]]$ at these roots gives the two factors $\Omega[[t]]$ of the integral closure of $\Omega[[X,Y]]/(q)$ in its total ring of fractions [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series, def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Thus the chart point indexed by $r_i$ is precisely the completed branch $X=r_iY$. Coefficient extension here means formal power series over the extended coefficient algebra, not the ordinary tensor product of an infinite power series ring. For every other invertible linear coordinate system $X',Y'$ for the same binary form in which the coefficient of $(X')^2$ is nonzero, the image of $Y'$ in $L[[t]]$ has leading coefficient a unit of $L$.

proof.text: Put $\beta=b/a$, $\gamma=c/a$ and $\Delta=\beta^2-4\gamma=(b^2-4ac)/a^2\ne0$. Multiplication by $a^{-1}$ does not change the defining principal ideal. Apply [lem-sfb-quadratic-homogeneous-substitution] to obtain the basis $1,z$ and relation $z^2=-\beta z-\gamma$. Apply [lem-sfb-quadratic-series-field-factors] to this monic quadratic: if it has a root in $F$, evaluation identifies $L$ with $F\times F$; otherwise $L$ is a degree-two field extension. The basis gives dimension two in either case.

source.place: Tag 0C4A (lemma-2-branches-delta-1), proof, Cases I and II; Tag 0CBU (remark-trivial-quadratic-extension).

proof.text:
In the field case, write an arbitrary element as $w=d+ez$ with $d,e\in F$. If $e=0$, its minimal polynomial is $T-d$, whose derivative is $1$. If $e
e0$, the basis $1,z$ implies $w
otin F$. Substitution shows that the monic quadratic $g(T)=(T-d)^2+ eta e(T-d)+\gamma e^2$ annihilates $w$. Its minimal polynomial, the monic generator of the evaluation kernel in [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], divides $g$ and cannot have degree one, hence equals $g$. The identity $g'(T)^2-4g(T)=e^2\Delta
e0$ shows that $g$ and $g'$ generate the unit ideal, so $g$ is separable. Thus every element is separable. This uses no division by $2$, and includes characteristic two. In the split case the two field factors are $F$ itself.

source.place: Tag 0CBT (remark-quadratic-extension), assertion that the algebra has separable degree two; explicit verification of separability by Q14.

proof.text: Fix $u\in L^\times$. For $n\ge1$ and $r\in L$, the identity $(rt^n)^2=(ut)(r^2u^{-1}t^{2n-1})$ is an identity in $H$: its second factor has positive degree. If a homogeneous prime contained $ut$, primality would therefore force every $rt^n$ into it, hence the whole irrelevant ideal. Such a prime is excluded from Proj by [def-nagata-affine-proj]. Consequently every point lies in $D_+(ut)$; an open subscheme containing every point is the whole scheme.

source.place: Tag 0CBT (remark-quadratic-extension), omitted equivalence with construction (3); explicit coefficient-chart computation by Q14.

proof.text: In the degree-zero localization [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], define $\psi(rt^n/(ut)^n)=r/u^n$ for $n\ge1$, and use the scalar inclusion on degree-zero constants. The element $ut$ is a non-zero-divisor in $L[t]$, since $u$ is a unit and multiplication by $t$ shifts coefficients. The localization equality between two homogeneous fractions therefore cancels to equality after cross multiplication; comparing coefficients gives $r/u^n=s/u^m$. Thus $\psi$ is well-defined. Common denominators show it preserves addition and multiplication. The map $\eta:L\to H[(ut)^{-1}]_0$ given by $s\mapsto(su)t/(ut)$ is a ring map: for products cancel $ut$ from $(su)t(s'u)t/(ut)^2$, and for the unit use $ut/(ut)=1$. Directly $\psi\eta=1$, and $\eta\psi(rt^n/(ut)^n)=rt^n/(ut)^n$ after multiplying numerator and denominator to degree $n+1$; constants satisfy the same identity. Hence these maps are inverse $F$-algebra isomorphisms. Apply [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open] to the degree-one element $ut$ and use step 3 to identify all of $\operatorname{Proj}H$ with $\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Tag 0CBT (remark-quadratic-extension), omitted equivalence with construction (3); explicit coefficient-chart computation by Q14.

proof.text: Let $\Omega/F$ be an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. The monic quadratic $p(T)=T^2+\beta T+\gamma$ has a root $r_1$ in $\Omega$. Set $r_2=-\beta-r_1$; then $p=(T-r_1)(T-r_2)$, and $(r_1-r_2)^2=\Delta\ne0$, so the roots are distinct and exhaust the roots of $a p$. Write $z_\Omega=z\otimes1$. The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] defines an $\Omega$-algebra map $\epsilon:L\otimes_F\Omega\to\Omega\times\Omega$ by $\epsilon((d+ez)\otimes\lambda)=(\lambda(d+er_1),\lambda(d+er_2))$. Multiplicativity follows from $p(z)=p(r_i)=0$. In the tensor algebra put $E_1=(z_\Omega-r_2)/(r_1-r_2)$ and $E_2=(r_1-z_\Omega)/(r_1-r_2)$. The quadratic relation gives $E_i^2=E_i$, $E_1E_2=0$, $E_1+E_2=1$ and $r_1E_1+r_2E_2=z_\Omega$. Thus $(v_1,v_2)\mapsto v_1E_1+v_2E_2$ is an inverse ring map: compositions fix $(1,0),(0,1)$ and fix $1,z_\Omega$, which span all pure tensors by the basis in step 1. This proves the asserted evaluation isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0CBT (remark-quadratic-extension), construction (1), and Tag 0CBU (remark-trivial-quadratic-extension), applied after coefficient extension; explicit evaluation formulas by Q14.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the geometric fibre of the $F$-scheme identified in step 4 is $\operatorname{Spec}(L\otimes_F\Omega)$. Step 5 identifies this with $\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega\times\Omega)$. A prime in this product contains exactly one of the idempotents $(1,0),(0,1)$, because their product is zero and their sum is one. It therefore is the kernel of exactly one projection to the field $\Omega$, whose only prime is zero [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. There are exactly two points. The coefficient coordinate $z$ is represented on the $ut$ chart by $(zu)t/(ut)$, and step 4 maps it to $z$; the two projections send it to $r_1,r_2$ respectively.

source.place: Tag 0CBT (remark-quadratic-extension), constructions (1) and (3), and Tag 0CBU (remark-trivial-quadratic-extension): geometric points.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-quadratic-series-integral-closure] over the field $\Omega$ to $aX^2+bXY+cY^2$: the nonzero discriminant stays nonzero under the field inclusion. It identifies the integral closure of $\Omega[[X,Y]]/(q)$ in its total ring of fractions with $(\Omega[Z]/(p))[[t]]$, through $X\mapsto z_\Omega t$, $Y\mapsto t$. The basis and evaluation maps of step 5 identify its coefficient algebra with $L\otimes_F\Omega\cong\Omega\times\Omega$. Applying these maps coefficient by coefficient gives an isomorphism to $\Omega[[t]]\times\Omega[[t]]$; this respects multiplication because each coefficient of a series product is a finite sum [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The two projections send $X,Y$ to $r_i t,t$. Their kernels are exactly $(X-r_iY)$: termwise use $X^jY^k-(r_iY)^jY^k=(X-r_iY)\sum_{h=0}^{j-1}X^{j-1-h}(r_iY)^hY^k$. For a series these sums define a series quotient, since only finitely many terms contribute in each total degree. Thus a series differs from its substitution at $X=r_iY$ by a multiple of $X-r_iY$, and the substituted series lies in $\Omega[[Y]]$, with $Y\mapsto t$ an isomorphism. These are precisely the two completed branches, labelled by the same evaluations as the chart points in step 6. No assertion identifies an ordinary tensor product of an infinite series ring with coefficient extension.

source.place: Tag 0C4A (lemma-2-branches-delta-1), proof, Cases I and II; Tag 0CBU (remark-trivial-quadratic-extension), branch interpretation.

proof.text: Write the other invertible linear coordinates as $X'=AX+BY$, $Y'=CX+DY$, with $\delta=AD-BC\ne0$. In the original normalization substitution, $Y'=(Cz+D)t$. Expressing the same form in $X',Y'$ gives its $(X')^2$ coefficient $a'=(aD^2-bDC+cC^2)/\delta^2$. Using the quadratic relation of step 1, compute $(Cz+D)(D-\beta C-Cz)=D^2-\beta CD+\gamma C^2=\delta^2a'/a$. The hypothesis $a'\ne0$ makes this scalar invertible in $F$. Therefore $Cz+D$ is a unit of $L$, with inverse $(D-\beta C-Cz)/(\delta^2a'/a)$. It is the leading coefficient of $Y'$ as a series in $t$, proving the final clause, including when $L$ is split or the characteristic is two.
